file_types.label: JavaScript
rules: Use ES modules with import/export.
Prefer named exports for reusable utilities.
Avoid global state and hidden side effects.
Keep browser-facing code build-compatible with the existing bundler.

file_types.label: Vue Single File Component
rules: Respect existing Vue 3 and Vuetify conventions.
Do not assume npm run serve or npm run dev.
Keep API calls out of visual components when a shared service exists.
Keep component state explicit and easy to debug.

file_types.label: SCSS
rules: Write SCSS, not scattered ad-hoc global CSS.
Use shared partials/modules for variables, mixins, tokens and functions.
Prefer @use and @forward over legacy @import.
Avoid random one-off class sprawl; create reusable semantic structure.
Keep design tokens centralized.

file_types.label: Python
rules: Use type hints for new functions.
Prefer pathlib for filesystem paths.
Keep Flask routes thin and push business logic into model/service layers.
Validate JSON, form, query, path and upload inputs.
Never log secrets or user binary payloads.

file_types.label: JSON
rules: Keep JSON valid and machine-readable.
Keep AI-readable configuration in English.
Do not store secrets in JSON.
Prefer flat extendable arrays with id fields over deeply nested objects.

file_types.label: Markdown
rules: Document what changed, why it changed and how to validate it.
Avoid outdated instructions.
Keep command examples copy-pasteable.

file_types.label: Shader
rules: Keep shader code deterministic and performance-aware.
Avoid expensive branches in hot fragment paths unless justified.
Preserve material input compatibility.
Document coordinate space and texture map assumptions.

file_types.label: Image Asset
rules: Do not overwrite source assets unless explicitly requested.
Preserve alpha, dimensions, color space and map purpose.
Write metadata for generated assets.
Keep generated assets out of source control unless explicitly intended.

file_types.label: TypeScript
rules: Prefer explicit types at public boundaries.
Do not introduce TypeScript migration unless the project already uses it or the user asks.
Keep Vue/ThreeJS types aligned with installed versions.

file_types.label: 3D Scene / Model Asset
rules: Do not overwrite original scene assets.
Preserve scale, units, material slots and texture links.
Use sidecar metadata for generated or converted assets.

file_types.label: Photoshop Document
rules: Treat PSD/PSB as source assets.
Preserve layer/group naming and non-destructive edit intent.
Export derivatives beside sources unless explicitly asked to overwrite.

file_types.label: Data Table
rules: Preserve headers and units.
Do not silently coerce currency, decimals or dates.
Document formulas used for derived values.

file_types.label: Localization / Translation
rules: Preserve message ids, keys and placeholders.
Translate values only when keys are code-facing identifiers.
Keep pluralization and interpolation syntax intact.

file_types.label: C# / Unity
rules: Respect Unity assembly and folder conventions when evidence exists.
Do not invent Unity package dependencies without selected stack context.

file_types.label: C++ Source
rules: Keep headers, source files and build configuration separated.
Prefer standard library facilities before adding dependencies.

file_types.label: C/C++ Header
rules: Keep public API boundaries small and explicit.
Avoid leaking implementation details through headers.

file_types.label: HTML
rules: Keep HTML semantic and accessible.
Do not inline large scripts or styles when project structure exists.

file_types.label: CSS
rules: Prefer shared tokens and component-scoped CSS where the framework supports it.
Avoid unrelated global class sprawl.

file_types.label: SVG
rules: Keep SVGs readable and metadata-light.
Preserve viewBox and semantic grouping when editing existing assets.

file_types.label: Shell Script
rules: Keep scripts target-scoped and reversible.
Use set -euo pipefail only when the script is compatible with it.
Do not embed secrets.

file_types.label: Dockerfile
rules: Keep images minimal and target-specific.
Do not copy dependency caches unless explicitly required.

file_types.label: YAML
rules: Preserve indentation and key order where humans maintain the file.
Do not store secrets in YAML.

file_types.label: Dart
rules: Keep widgets small and state ownership explicit.
Do not assume Flutter SDK commands unless the selected stack or project evidence provides them.

file_types.label: C Source
rules: Keep headers and source files separated.
Avoid undefined behavior and document ownership/lifetime rules.

file_types.label: TOML config
rules: Use for pyproject.toml and tool configuration manifests.

file_types.label: Environment template
rules: Never store real secrets; use placeholders only.

file_types.label: SQL schema/query
rules: Keep migrations, seed data and ad-hoc queries separated.

file_types.label: CMake config
rules: Keep build options explicit and platform-neutral where possible.

file_types.label: Makefile
rules: Use target-scoped commands and document side effects.

file_types.label: Go source
rules: Respect module boundaries and go.mod ownership.

file_types.label: Rust source
rules: Respect Cargo manifest and crate boundaries.

file_types.label: PHP source
rules: Respect composer.json dependency ownership.

file_types.label: Ruby source
rules: Respect Gemfile dependency ownership.

file_types.label: C# project file
rules: Treat project references and package references as manifest evidence.

file_types.label: Jupyter notebook
rules: Keep notebooks reproducible; mirror dependencies in environment.yml or requirements.txt.

file_types.label: R source
rules: Document package setup and data provenance.

file_types.label: Protocol Buffer
rules: Keep generated code separate from source schema.

file_types.label: Dependency lock file
rules: Treat lock files as generated/pinned dependency evidence.

file_types.label: Plain text
rules: Keep text readable and line-ending stable.
Use plain text boxes for metadata; do not insert language-specific comment syntax.

file_type_selection_rule: Targets may select multiple file_types. Active rules, hooks, weights and boilerplates must be reduced to the selected file types.
